topic: RC-404 is live again: sessions can publish by writing into a listed folder, and wildcards let them create matching folders
detail: Security audit of SP-076 (medium M2, design under D-65). A folder a public_paths pattern lists is trusted as written: any job's session can write files there and register it as a source, and the sources refresh places them in public; a listed folder with no .git needs no other proof. With '*' or '**' a session can also create a new folder the pattern matches (e.g. ~/code/new/docs under ~/code/*/docs). This is the risk the user accepted as RC-404 for declared folders, which said to review it when public_paths exists. Documented in docs/internals/config.md. The independent verifier adds: the sources walk follows a .md symlink to any file inside the walked folder, so a link in an exact listed folder can index a file from an unlisted subfolder under the link's path, again only by someone who can write into the listed folder. Possible mitigations: require a GitHub repo verified public (and only git-tracked files) for wildcard matches; accept only operator-registered sources under public_paths; SP-046 sandbox rules denying job sessions writes to listed folders; warn in 'orch spaces diff' when a pattern holds '*' or '**'. Recommendation: keep as accepted risk now, and have SP-046 deny job-session writes to listed folders.
note: Settled by the user on 2026-11-14 with option (a): see D-73. Accepted as RC-404's accepted risk extended; the sandbox follow-up is RC-805.
